# Translink Express makes four senior appointments

Leicestershire logistics firm Translink Express Logistics has made four senior appointments following 32 per cent growth over the past two years.

Lee Barrett has been promoted to head of traffic; Dan Green takes the newly created role of head of project management; and Shanice Walsh becomes head of operations.

Ryan Wallis has also joined the family-owned business as head of warehousing.

The new management team will take responsibility for the day-to-day running of Translink Express, allowing its directors to focus more closely on long-term strategy as the business approaches its 40th anniversary.

Chris Hobbis, director at Translink Express Logistics, said: “In two years we’ve seen record growth – just shy of 32 per cent, which is phenomenal.

“The growth is twofold, coming from new customers and existing customers expanding the range of services they use from us.

Translink Express Logistics announces four senior leadership appointments and plans to transform 66,000 sq. ft premises into huge pallet sortation centre

Translink Express Logistics announces four senior leadership appointments and plans to transform 66,000 sq. ft premises into huge pallet sortation centre

A Leicestershire logistics firm which has grown by a record 32 per cent over the last two years has made four senior leadership appointments as it approaches its 40th anniversary.

Translink Express Logistics has promoted three members of its team to senior roles, with Lee Barrett becoming Head of Traffic; Dan Green taking up a newly created position of Head of Project Management and Shanice Walsh promoted to Head of Operations.

The fourth appointment is a new hire, with Ryan Wallis joining the firm as Head of Warehousing.

# Route2 Logistics opens new Coatbridge depot

 by Transport News | Aug 13, 2026 | Hot News

### Route2 Logistics has officially opened its new depot in Coatbridge, marking a major milestone in the continued growth of the specialist haulage and pallet distribution business.

The new 22,000sq ft facility provides additional warehousing, yard space and vehicle capacity, creating a significant new operational base for Route2 in the West of Scotland and complementing its Dunfermline operation.

The company said the new site creates a stronger Scotland-based network, enabling the business to provide faster lead times, greater capacity and greater flexibility for companies delivering products to customers across Scotland.

Marc Batey, commercial manager at Route2 Logistics, said: “Dunfermline has been our foundation for Route2 in the East of Scotland. Opening a depot further West is the next step in building a stronger, more connected Scottish network.

“Coatbridge puts us right in the heart of the Central Belt and gives us a much stronger position from which to serve customers across Scotland.”
